title: Quantum Wave-Particle Duality in Free-Electron--Free-Electron Entanglement
authors: Du Ran, Jing-Yi Liu, Dan Jin, Peng-Yu Su, Reuven Ianconescu, Shuai Liu, Avraham Gover
abstract: Point-particle descriptions of electron-electron interaction omit the coherent longitudinal extent of a free-electron quantum wave packet (QEW). A relativistic two-electron wave-packet theory identifies the longitudinal QEW size as a direct control parameter for entanglement generated by mutual electromagnetic coupling. For two electrons in spatially separated paths, the quadratic interaction phase gives a dimensionless entangling parameter $\Gee$ and the logarithmic negativity $\EN=\operatorname{arsinh}(\Gee)/\ln2$. Full time-dependent Schrödinger equation calculations confirm the scaling for narrow QEWs and reveal higher-order Coulomb effects at larger spatial extent. Free drift increases the interaction-point QEW width while preserving the momentum probability distribution, thereby enhancing the subsequently generated entanglement. The results establish a direct connection between free-electron wave-particle duality and bipartite entanglement.
summary: This theoretical paper connects the physical concept of free-electron wave packet size to bipartite entanglement generated by Coulomb interaction. By solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, the authors show that entanglement scales with the square of the QEW width, providing a novel mechanism for controlling quantum correlations using spatial wave-packet engineering.
main_problem: The study aims to establish a direct, quantifiable link between the free-electron wave-particle duality—characterized by the longitudinal extent of the quantum wave packet (QEW)—and the bipartite entanglement generated via mutual electromagnetic coupling.
main_result: The entanglement strength scales directly with the square of the QEW width ($\Gamma_{	ext{ee}} \propto \sigma_z^2$), demonstrating that spatial control over the free electron wave packet can govern quantum correlations. Furthermore, higher-order effects reveal a finite entangling channel even when the quadratic term vanishes.
method: The research employs analytical approximations (quadratic phase gate) combined with numerical solutions of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE) using split-operator FFT methods to calculate entanglement measures like logarithmic negativity ($E_N$).
model_or_system: The model consists of two free electrons propagating along spatially separated paths, interacting via a Coulomb potential. The system dynamics are governed by the TDSE, which is analyzed in terms of center-of-mass and relative coordinates.
key_observables: Logarithmic Negativity ($E_N$), Dimensionless entangling parameter ($\Gamma_{	ext{ee}}$), Longitudinal QEW width ($\sigma_z$).
important_parameters: QEW longitudinal width ($\sigma_z$), Free drift length ($L_D$), Interaction potential parameters ($\gamma$, $\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes spatially separated propagation modes and that interaction-induced transverse displacements are small compared to path separation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of entanglement on QEW width, scaling with the effective entangling parameter; they also show how free drift expands the wave packet while maintaining momentum distribution, and compare quadratic vs. full TDSE results at specific nodes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model using the Hamiltonian and TDSE. It then derives analytical scalings based on the quadratic interaction phase, confirms these with numerical simulations across varying QEW widths, and finally explores how free drift and higher-order terms modify this entanglement scaling.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental concepts from quantum optics (wave-particle duality) into condensed matter/quantum information by showing that a geometric property of the electron wave function directly controls measurable quantum correlations (entanglement).
